goal: Makes writing settings.json and banlist.json atomic so an interrupted or failed write can't leave a truncated or corrupted file on disk.
Benefits node operators and future maintainers relying on those files being consistent after crashes or write errors.
reviewability: Latest push resolved the naming asymmetry reviewers flagged and no material request is open.
agreement: Positive: two reviewers engaged substantively and both non-blocking concerns were addressed in later pushes (winterrdog, Herb-ops).
A naming-consistency question (WriteJson vs ReadSettings) was resolved when the author adopted the reviewer's suggested direction (winterrdog, kevkevinpal).

categories.name: utils
why: P3 because it hardens a narrow but real correctness gap: a failed or interrupted write to settings.json or banlist.json could previously leave a truncated file that fails to parse on next start.
Impact is bounded to two config-like files rather than a widely-hit code path, so it is worthwhile but not urgent.

result.summary: This PR renames common::WriteSettings to WriteJson and changes it to write to a `path.tmp` file and RenameOver() it into the destination, so a failed or interrupted write cannot leave a truncated settings.json or banlist.json. It also updates both current callers (ArgsManager and CBanDB) to use the unified atomic helper instead of each doing their own tmp+rename dance, and adds unit tests covering the roundtrip, tmp-file cleanup on success, and stable tmp-file reuse on repeated rename failures.
result.problem: Previously, a write to settings.json (via ArgsManager) already used a tmp+rename pattern implemented at the call site, but banlist.json (via CBanDB) wrote directly to the live file, so a crash or I/O failure mid-write could leave a truncated or corrupted banlist.json that fails to parse on the next startup. Node operators who hit an interrupted write would face a broken config or ban list.

resolved_concerns: Herb-ops noted the original test didn't actually verify rename behavior and that error messages said 'settings file' for the generic helper; addressed by rewording messages and later tests.

winterrdog raised a footgun concern (a future caller could bypass atomic writing) and proposed making the helper always atomic (approach B); author adopted this by making WriteJson always do tmp+rename.

winterrdog asked whether failed writes should clean up the leftover .tmp file; author explained the tmp path is stable so it doesn't accumulate, and added a test proving this; winterrdog did not push back further.

winterrdog flagged a naming asymmetry between WriteJson and ReadSettings; author agreed and pushed a commit adopting the simplest fix (keep ReadSettings/WriteSettings naming, i.e. approach A), noting a follow-up could pursue full extraction later.

Impact is limited to two auxiliary files (not the wallet or chainstate), and no incident report is cited, so it is a solid reliability fix rather than a category-critical one.

uncertainties: Whether any real-world corruption of banlist.json or settings.json has actually been reported, versus this being a preventive hardening measure, is not stated in the discussion.
Long-term naming/design direction (approach C, fully generic JSON helpers) is left for a future PR; current PR's scope is judged as-is.
result.card: This PR renames common::WriteSettings to WriteJson and makes it always write via a `.tmp` file plus RenameOver(), so an interrupted or failed write cannot leave a truncated settings.json or banlist.json; CBanDB previously wrote banlist.json directly to the live path, which is the corruption hazard this closes. Two reviewers (winterrdog, Herb-ops) engaged substantively; each raised concrete concerns (test not actually verifying rename behavior, generic error-message wording, a footgun in an earlier two-function design, and a naming asymmetry between WriteJson and ReadSettings), and the author addressed all of them across several pushes, with winterrdog giving an approach ACK on the reworked version. The latest push (2026-09-10) resolved the last open naming discussion, leaving nothing material outstanding, so the PR is ready for review now. No dependencies block it; a possible follow-up to fully separate generic JSON helpers from settings-specific logic was discussed and deferred. Impact is a bounded reliability improvement to two auxiliary files rather than a widely-felt correctness fix.
